newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai '97 soymeal imports seen up at 1.2 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Thai '97 soymeal imports seen up at 1.2 mln tonnes.

text.p: Thai soymeal imports will probably rise to 1.2 million tonnes in 1997 from around one million tonnes last year, the director of the Thai Feed Mill Association said on Tuesday.
Somchai Kungsamutr told a feed ingredients conference in Singapore that a reduction in soymeal import duties to 10 percent from 15 percent will boost imports.
"We forsee imports of soybean meal in 1997 to grow to at least 1.2 million tonnes," he said, adding this was due mainly to increased feed demand from the poultry and pork industry.

The per capita consumption of chickens is likely to rise to 11.96 kg in 1997 against 11.43 kg last year. Per capita consumption of pork is also expected to increase to 15.81 kg this year against 15.23 kg in 1996.
The chicken population is seen expanding to 850 million this year from 810 million and will grow to 1.1 billion head by 2000, Somchai said.
The live hog population should rise to 13.4 million head by 2000 from the current 10.2 million head, he added.
